solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A fault not long showing up

parts.note: something not long is short
showing up means arriving, coming

explanation.surface: Someone admits to a flaw that has only recently surfaced.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortcoming is a defect or failing in a person or thing, so it is a fault.

clue.text: After work rushed in so as to see the entertainer

indicators.note: in means the following pieces are placed inside the word so

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: after means rushed comes after the work piece

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
rushed means ran

explanation.surface: Someone hurries after their shift so they can catch a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is a singer, one kind of entertainer.

clue.text: Plant seen in neat border

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
a lip is a rim or border

explanation.surface: A plant is noticed growing in a tidy flowerbed edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy, but it is the old word for cattle; 'seen in' is just a link, not a hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxlip is a wild flowering plant related to the primrose and cowslip.

clue.text: He heals, adjusting his patter accordingly

indicators.note: adjusting the words his patter means rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A healer tailors his sales talk to suit the client.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist treats patients, so is someone who heals.

clue.text: Forget to order vermouth

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
IT is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: A bartender fails to put in a request for a martini ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin and it' is a British cocktail of gin and Italian vermouth, hence IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to leave it out, as when you forget it.

clue.text: Lie in bed suffering, not fit enough to eat

indicators.note: suffering suggests the words lie in bed are in a bad way, so jumbled

explanation.surface: An invalid lies in bed, too unwell to eat a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Inedible food is unfit for eating.

clue.text: We'd be lost without him!

parts.note: a heartfelt tribute that literally describes the person who leads travellers along the way

explanation.definitionFit: A guide is someone who shows the way, without whom travellers would literally get lost.

clue.text: Make converse?

parts.note: the converse, or opposite, of making something is unmaking it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Converse' looks like a verb meaning chat, but here it is the noun for an opposite: the reverse of make.
explanation.definitionFit: Destroying is the opposite of making or creating something.

clue.text: Cause of cracks that may bring the house down

definitions.text: Cause of cracks that may bring the house down

parts.words: Cause of cracks that may bring the house down
parts.note: cracks here are wisecracks, and bringing the house down is earning huge laughter, not a building collapsing

explanation.definitionFit: A comedian makes wisecracks and can bring the house down with laughter in a theatre.

clue.text: Awfully repulsive — crush

indicators.note: awfully suggests the word repulsive is badly mangled, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something is described as dreadfully repellent, with a crushing verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: To pulverise is to grind to powder, a forceful synonym of crush.

clue.text: Restrictions for members in clubs

definitions.meaning: fetters or shackles put on a prisoner restrict movement
a golfer's set of clubs includes these metal-headed members

explanation.definitionFit: Irons are shackles for prisoners, and also the iron-headed golf clubs in a golfer's bag.

clue.text: How's that for charm?

definitions.meaning: the cricketers' cry to the umpire asking for a batsman to be given out is an ...
charm as a noun means attractiveness or allure

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, fielders shout 'How's that?' (often 'Howzat') to ask the umpire for a dismissal; this is called an appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: An appeal is the fielders' formal request in cricket, and also the allure or attractiveness a thing has.

clue.text: Take out file and look for one with non-hereditary entitlement

indicators.note: take out here suggests the word file is taken apart and remade, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: to peer is to look closely, as when searching for something

explanation.surface: A clerk removes a document and searches for someone with a title that will not pass to heirs.
explanation.walkthrough: A life peer is a member of the British House of Lords whose title lapses at death rather than passing to an heir.
explanation.definitionFit: A life peer holds a title for life only, so the entitlement is not hereditary.

clue.text: Road-works in order

indicators.note: works implies the word road is dug up and reworked, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Roadworks are carried out in an orderly sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to decree or command something, a formal sense of order as a verb.

clue.text: A double first

parts.note: not a university degree of top honours but two competitors finishing first together

explanation.walkthrough: A double first is a British top-class degree in two subjects; here it means a race tied for first place.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead heat is a race in which two finish exactly level, so both come first.

clue.text: Expedition to the French metropolis goes round river

parts.note: in French, to the (feminine) is a la

indicators.note: goes round means the city word encircles the river letter

parts.note: a metropolis is a big city

explanation.surface: A journey to a French city takes a route around a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expedition' looks like a journey, matching the surface trip, but here it means speed or promptness.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition can mean speed and promptness in action, which is what alacrity means.

clue.text: Best advertisement for a pastry?

parts.note: the cream of something is the best part
a puff is a piece of promotional publicity

explanation.surface: A baker wonders which cake would best promote the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream puff is a light choux pastry filled with cream.

clue.text: Remove it, as ordered, for extra pay

indicators.note: as ordered signals the words remove it are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A worker is told to cancel a bonus payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtime is the extra payment for hours worked beyond the normal ones.

clue.text: I can't change, I've become idle

indicators.note: change following the word can't signals that its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the contraction I've, apostrophe dropped, supplies its letters as written

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that, unable to alter their ways, they have grown lazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Inactive means not doing anything, which is the sense of idle here.

clue.text: Fire confined to part of church

parts.note: confined to a place is in it
a spire is the tall pointed top of a church tower

explanation.surface: A blaze is contained within a section of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like a blaze, but it is a verb meaning to enthuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone up is to inspire them, filling them with enthusiasm.

clue.text: Be inclined to shelter in the garden perhaps

definitions.meaning: to be inclined is to lean towards something
a simple shed propped against a wall, often found in a garden

explanation.definitionFit: Lean to as a phrase means tend towards, and a lean-to is a shed built against a wall.

clue.text: Regular soldier?

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means neat and regular
a soldier who carries orders or attends an officer, or a hospital attendant

explanation.definitionFit: Orderly means tidy and regular, and an orderly is a soldier attending an officer.

clue.text: Erudite professors or their proteges perhaps

definitions.meaning: pupils holding scholarships are also called by this name

explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is both a learned academic and a student who holds a scholarship.

clue.text: Rings to see what the film's about in write-up

indicators.note: in a down clue a write-up means the word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: film is wound about a spool

explanation.surface: A reviewer circles the plot in their write-up of a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' here means around: film is wound around a spool.
explanation.definitionFit: Loops are rings or circles, as in a loop of rope.

clue.text: Morning spent being entertained

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for morning, ante meridiem
spent means used up

explanation.surface: A morning gone by while someone was being diverted.
explanation.definitionFit: To be amused is to be entertained or diverted.

clue.text: Point to inferior scent

parts.note: S is south, a point of the compass
poor means of low quality, inferior

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a perfume is second-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the track or scent left by an animal, followed by hunters.

clue.text: A shade depressed

definitions.meaning: a shade is a colour, and this is one
feeling depressed is feeling low or down

explanation.definitionFit: Blue is a colour, and feeling blue means feeling sad or depressed.

clue.text: State aid distributed by Home Office

indicators.note: distributed suggests aid is spread about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for the Home Office, the UK interior ministry

explanation.surface: Government department hands out assistance across a region.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the states of the USA, an example of a state.

clue.text: Bad temper resulting from sick jokes

parts.note: sick means ill
jokes collectively are humour

explanation.surface: Someone's anger is caused by tasteless, sick jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill humour is a bad mood or irritable temper.

clue.text: The Greeks probably regarded it as a capital investment

definitions.text: The Greeks probably regarded it as a capital investment

parts.words: The Greeks probably regarded it as a capital investment
parts.note: investment in the military sense is besieging a city; the Greeks in legend surrounded a capital city for ten years

explanation.walkthrough: 'Investment' looks financial, but it is the old military word for surrounding a town; 'capital' is a chief city, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: The ten-year Greek blockade of the city of Priam was a military investment of a capital.
